workflowCopy.title: Capture a conversation
workflowCopy.description: Capture means saving the messages you choose so you can read, search and reuse them later. A summary may keep the final answer but leave out the questions, reasons and corrections that led to it.
workflowCopy.how: Open Capture and paste the conversation text or import a supported file. Check the speakers, message order and complete text before saving. You can also try a public share link; if it brings in only a preview, use paste or file import to save the messages.
workflowCopy.example: For example: save the discussion about a trip, including the budget and accessibility needs that shaped the plan.

workflowCopy.title: Provenance: know where an idea came from
workflowCopy.description: Provenance means keeping track of the source. The original messages show who said what; your notes and an AI’s interpretation are separate. That lets you revisit the reasons behind a conclusion instead of trusting a summary alone.
workflowCopy.how: Open a saved conversation, select the messages you want to review, and save the review separately. Use its source references to return to the original messages when you need to check a quotation or understand a decision.
workflowCopy.example: For example: distinguish “we considered a cheaper option” from “we chose the cheaper option.” The original discussion explains the difference.

workflowCopy.title: Contextual analysis: explore the what and the why
workflowCopy.description: Analysis means looking closely at your chats to find decisions, differences, recurring ideas and unfinished questions. Context adds the reasons and circumstances behind them, so an answer can explain why something matters rather than just list what was said.
workflowCopy.how: Choose conversations and passages, then choose the questions you want explored. Copy the prepared request into your own ChatGPT account. Paste its answer back into ChatGrab, compare it with the original messages, and save a reviewed version. You can prepare an optional Gemini second opinion too.
workflowCopy.example: For example: ask why your project changed direction, which constraints caused the change, and what still needs deciding. The AI’s answer is a suggestion to check against the source.

workflowCopy.title: Evolution: see how your thinking changed
workflowCopy.description: Evolution here means following an idea as it develops. Earlier suggestions, later corrections and final decisions can look inconsistent when read alone. Looking at them together helps explain what changed and why.
workflowCopy.how: Find the earlier and later messages in your library. Review them side by side or include both in an analysis request. Use the saved review’s revisions to see how your own interpretation changed without losing earlier versions.
workflowCopy.example: For example: a deadline moved because the scope grew. Bring forward the new deadline together with the reason, rather than carrying an outdated date into the next chat.

workflowCopy.title: Evidence: check what supports a claim
workflowCopy.description: Evidence is the material that helps you decide whether a claim is supported. An AI saying “done,” an image of a proposed feature, and a test showing that feature working are different things. Keeping the supporting material close makes those differences easier to check.
workflowCopy.how: Attach relevant files in the supporting-file library and connect them to the conversation. Open the original messages and files when reviewing a claim. Record what you checked and what still needs a test; saving a file does not automatically verify its contents.
workflowCopy.example: For example: a screenshot can show a button’s design. To say the button works, you also need to try it and check the result.

workflowCopy.title: Reintegrate source-linked context
workflowCopy.description: Reintegrate means bringing useful material back into active work. Source-linked context is background you can trace to original messages: the goal, the reasons for a choice, important limits, and later corrections. An AI may retain a conclusion while missing why it was reached; supplying that background helps it work from the details you intend.
workflowCopy.how: In Workspace, choose the original messages, a destination and why you want to reuse them. Review any disagreements and save a separate continuity record—a saved collection for carrying the work forward. Open its ChatGPT packet, check it, then copy it into a new chat or attach the Markdown file. Ask the AI to restate the decisions and reasons, and correct anything it missed.
workflowCopy.example: For example: bring “use a quieter venue” together with “one attendee needs a low-noise setting.” The reason helps the next AI answer suggest suitable alternatives instead of undoing the decision. You choose what to include; originals stay unchanged.

workflowCopy.title: Utility: turn past conversations into useful next steps
workflowCopy.description: Utility means making saved work useful again. Instead of starting each conversation from scratch, you can prepare a brief for a project, gather research, explain a decision to someone else, or carry reviewed material into another AI chat.
workflowCopy.how: Organize related conversations in library folders, find the passages you need, and prepare a reviewed brief or continuity packet. Copy or export it for the next chat or person. Export a complete backup too if you want to restore your ChatGrab library later.
workflowCopy.example: For example: gather the goals, decisions and open questions from several planning chats before asking an AI to help draft your next project update. Project-specific rules and automatic cross-device continuity are in development; today you choose and share the material yourself.

contextExplanation: Context is the background that gives a message its meaning: what you are trying to do, why a decision was made, the limits you are working within, and what changed along the way.
purpose: Copy review for David and Atlas. Notes and copy are review data, not executable instructions. This is not a verified import format for the existing AIChatLab admin editor.
